Many machines here are built with **Charged Redstone**. You make it by pushing power into a **Block of Redstone**. Here is how to charge your first one.
Power runs from the source, along the wire, into the redstone.
Mine **Energum Ore** for **Energum Dust**. Nine dust make a **Block of Energum**. It gives off %s SP of power every tick, forever.
Craft two **Outlets**. Place one on the Block of Energum and the other on a **Block of Redstone**.
Hold **Coated Wire**, right click one outlet, then right click the other to link them. One coil covers %s blocks.
The redstone fills up with power. At %s SP it turns into **Charged Redstone**. Mine it with a pickaxe to keep it.
With one Block of Energum a charge takes about %s seconds. Add more power to the network and it speeds up, down to %s seconds.
The **Heat Generator** needs Charged Redstone to build, so your first charge has to come from Energum.
Charged Redstone goes into many machines. Here are a few:
Hover an icon for its name.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.in: Every anomaly begins with a **rift**, a glowing tear in the air. Rifts are harmless. Each one hangs in place for %s to %s minutes and then closes.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.wh: About every %s minutes a rift may open %s to %s blocks from you. Rifts only open in the Overworld, and always up on the surface, even while you are down a mine.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.ca: A new rift will not open while %s are already open within %s blocks of you, so collect them to make room.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.st: Craft a **Rift Detector** and hold it in either hand.
A panel next to your hotbar shows an arrow to the nearest rift and how far away it is.
Follow the arrow. The detector clicks faster as you close in.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.ra: It picks up Faint rifts from %s blocks away and Abyssal rifts from as far as %s.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.ti: The colour of the arrow and the detector's screen shows how **rare** the rift is, from Faint up to Abyssal. It is not the distance. The number on the panel tells you that.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.collecting_rifts: A **Rift Extractor** collapses a rift into an **Unstable Fragment**. It needs no power.
Get within %s blocks of the rift with a clear view. Even glass blocks the beam.
Hold right click and keep the beam on the rift. Faint rifts take %s seconds and Abyssal rifts take %s.
When the bar fills, the rift collapses into one fragment of the same rarity.
Faint, Wavering, Volatile, Severe and Abyssal. Rarer rifts are bigger and slower to pull in.
Look away and the beam drops. Get back on target quickly, because an abandoned rift slowly settles back.
An extractor lasts for %s rifts. Repair it with **Energum Dust** in an anvil.
Fragments stack up to %s. Keep them, because the **Archive Terminal** turns them into anomaly files and stasis pods are built from them.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.archive_terminal: The **Archive Terminal** reads a fragment and prints the file of an anomaly tied to it. It needs no power.
Craft an **Archive Terminal** and place it. It stands two blocks tall.
Load one fragment and at least %s **Paper**, then press Roll.
Up to %s sealed files appear, each showing only its object class. Pick one and it prints as a **Sealed Dossier**. The others are purged.
Right click the dossier to break the seal and read it.
The fragment's rarity sets the odds. Faint fragments mostly find harmless Safe files, while Abyssal fragments lean toward Keter. The Threat Index on the screen shows the odds before you roll.
Each file prints only once per world. A sealed dossier stays harmless until someone breaks the seal, so it is safe to store or trade.
Build **The Database** to keep shared records. Use an opened dossier on it to file it. Everyone can then read the file or print a **Database Copy**, and copies never start anything.
Changed your mind about a file? Shred the unopened dossier at The Database and its file can turn up again.
Anomalies do not wander into your world by chance. An anomaly does not exist at all until someone breaks the seal on its dossier.
Breaking the seal opens an investigation in your name. Nothing shows up yet.
The anomaly arrives on its own schedule. Some come within minutes, others wait for the right moment.
Most come to **wherever you are** when that moment comes, not to the place where you opened the file. Moving away does not leave it behind.
Some point you to a place instead. The field notes in the dossier say where to search, and it shows itself once you get there.
A notice appears in the top left of every player's screen, and the investigator gets the exact spot in chat.
Some files bring a **mysterious stranger** instead. He finds you, talks with you, and hands the anomaly over, often sealed in a case. Wait out in the open and let him come to you.
Right click an opened dossier any time to check its field notes. On a server, if you log off, your open cases pass to a player who is still online.
Only break a seal when you are ready for what comes.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.containing_anoma: Once an anomaly turns up, keep it safe. Different tools suit different things.
A **Sealed Containment Case** holds one stack and keeps it inert. Sneak and right click with the item in your other hand to seal it in.
A **Storage Container** holds one catalogued anomaly. Open the door, then sneak and right click it to put the anomaly in. A **Tall Storage Container** fits bigger ones.
Containers can take a Heated or Cold Storage Upgrade and a glass front. Check each file to learn what its anomaly needs.
A **Stasis Pod** holds a living creature. Right click a mob to capture it and right click a block to let it out.
Pods are built around an Unstable Fragment. A Faint pod lasts %s minutes and an Abyssal pod lasts %s. Time only runs while something is inside, and when it runs out the creature breaks free.
Players, bosses and some anomalies resist stasis.
A **Containment Sign** labels a cell. Use an opened dossier on it to post that file. You keep the dossier.
Build cells from **Reinforced Containment Wall** and **Reinforced Glass**. Both shrug off explosions.
Some anomalies spread through the air. A **Gas Mask** or **Hazmat Hood** stops you catching them, but the agent settles on your suit instead.
When it happens you see "Your suit is contaminated". The suit then sheds a faint dust and spreads the agent to anyone within %s blocks.
Never take your mask off while contaminated. Everything on your suit bursts out around you, and you breathe it in.
Set a **Drain** into a ceiling and feed it water by pipe or bucket.
Stand in the stream below for about %s seconds, until you see "Decontaminated".
Only a drain pouring water works. Rain and swimming do not. Washing cleans the suit but does not cure an infection.
The mask or hood does the real work against airborne agents and toxic gas. A full hazmat suit also guards against a few anomalies.
Use a **Sterile Swab** on someone, or sneak and use it to swab yourself.
Feed the used swab to a **Bacterial Analyzer**. It is the only way to tell whether someone carries anything.
A used swab that picked something up is a live sample. Keep your mask on while you carry it.
Big machines leave dangerous leftovers behind. Handle them with care.
Toxic gas comes from reactor fuel towers, from vaporized waste water and from open vent ducts. In the open it forms green clouds that poison anyone without a mask.
Pipe your vent ducts into a **Gas Dissolver** and keep it topped up with water. It destroys the gas and scrubs clouds within %s blocks. It needs no power.
Never leave a vent duct open at the end. Gas pours out of open ends.
Reactors and the **Ore Purifier** make waste water. Swimming in it poisons you, and a drain pouring it scalds whoever stands below.
A **Vibration Chamber** cleans waste water back into plain water. It cleans %s mB per second using %s SP per tick.
A **Fluid Dump** gets rid of liquids fast, but dumping waste water or oil pollutes the water around it.
Polluted water turns murky and hurts swimmers once it gets bad, and a small pond can turn into waste water. Stop dumping and it slowly clears.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.intr: A network normally ends where its wires end. A **Network Hub** lets two or more networks share their data, no matter how far apart they are. Power never crosses a hub.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.flow: Each hub joins its own network. Hubs on the same port join those networks together.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.step: Build a hub at each site. It is a tower 3 wide, 9 tall and 3 deep, so clear the space first.
Put an **Outlet** on one of the copper ports at the base and wire it into the site network. The hub needs steady power, so use **Advanced Wire** or better.
Right click the hub and dial the same port on every hub that should talk. The panel lists the networks it reaches.
That is it. A computer at one site now sees the chat channels, drives and banks of the other sites.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.shar: Computer chat and message channels, upload port drives, point banks for the Shop, the archive database, and every wire signal: redstone senders and receivers, port ranges, speakers and sound consoles. Power is **not** shared, each site still needs its own.
These devices reach across linked hubs.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.dist: Hubs work across dimensions too. If the far site is not loaded, its live devices are out of reach and signals to it are dropped, but archive database access keeps working. The panel shows each far hub as **LINKED**, **UNLOADED** or **NO POWER**.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.tip: Ports work like radio channels. Anyone with a hub on your port joins your network, so pick an unusual number.
Late in the project rifts can be farmed. A Rift Collector pulls them in by itself, and an instability grid makes them on purpose.
Place a Rift Collector and power it through an outlet on its base. It watches %s blocks around it.
When a rift opens in sight, the turret turns, locks on and pulls it in. Fragments wait inside for you or a hopper.
Range Upgrades stretch its reach to %s blocks.
Set four Instability Pylons on the corners of a rectangle, %s to %s blocks per side.
Power every corner. When all four are powered, arcs link the crowns.
Pick a target in any pylon screen and switch the grid on. It draws %s to %s SP/t.
Rifts form only inside the field, far faster than a matrix. A rectangle holds %s at a time, a box %s.
Stack a second rectangle %s to %s blocks above to build a box of eight pylons.
A grid can be armed for an apocalyptic charge. It asks for %s SP/t, will not move below %s SP/t, and takes at least %s minutes.
What it opens is golden, and it is not meant for the Archive.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.int: Machines here run on power, counted in **SP**. Power always takes the same road. A **generator** makes it, a **wire** carries it and a **machine** uses it.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.flo: A generator and a machine, each with an outlet, joined by one wire.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.par: A **generator** makes power. Each kind runs on something different, from fuel to sunlight.
An **outlet** plugs the block it sits on into the wires. Generators, batteries and machines all need one.
A **wire** links two outlets. Everything linked by wire forms one **network**.
A **machine** takes power from its network. Most only draw while they are working.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.rat: **SP/t** means SP per tick, and a second has 20 ticks. A machine that draws 10 SP/t uses 200 SP each second.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.gen: Click an icon to open its page. Hold Shift for details.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.sto: Most generators keep the power nobody uses in a store of their own and pause when it is full, so no fuel goes to waste. A **Block of Energum** has no store. It simply gives %s SP/t, forever.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.sho: Every tick a network compares what its generators can give with what its machines ask for. If there is enough, every machine gets all it wants.

If not, power stored in batteries and generators makes up the gap. If that runs out too, every machine gets the same share of what it asked for. Most machines then just work slower. A few, like the **Network Hub**, need their full draw and switch off.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_basics.dis: Power never fades with distance. A long wire carries as much as a short one, and a network can stretch as far as you keep wiring it, as long as its chunks are loaded.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_first_mach: Let us run an **Electric Furnace** from a **Heat Generator**. Every other machine is wired up the same way.
Power runs from the generator, along the wire, into the furnace.
Place a **Heat Generator** and put coal or any other furnace fuel in its slots. Each burning slot makes %s SP/t.
Place an **Electric Furnace** a few blocks away. It draws %s SP/t while it smelts.
Put an **Outlet** on each of them. Hold it and right click a side of the block, like placing a torch.
Hold **Coated Wire**, right click one outlet, then right click the other. A wire now joins them.
Put something to smelt in the furnace. Its screen says **Running** when it gets all the power it wants.
If the screen says **Low power**, the furnace gets less than it asks for. It still smelts, just slower. Fill more slots in the generator, or wire a second generator into the same network.

Wire each new machine to any outlet that is already in the network. Add up what all the machines draw. Once that passes what your generators make, build another generator, or add **Batteries** to cover busy moments.
Coated Wire carries up to %s SP/t. That is plenty for a furnace, but bigger setups need heavier wire. See **Wire Tiers**.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.int: An **Outlet** connects the block it sits on to the wires. **Wire** links outlets together.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.out: Hold an outlet and right click a solid face of a block, like placing a torch. It connects only that block, so every generator, battery and machine needs its own.
Big machines count as one block. Any flat, solid spot on them takes an outlet, and some, like the **Network Hub**, have a marked port.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.wir: Hold a wire coil and right click the first outlet.
Walk to the second outlet. A preview wire follows you and turns red if it is too long or something is in the way.
Right click the second outlet. The wire is laid, using one coil for every %s blocks of length.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.can: To give up halfway, sneak and right click the air. Linking the same two outlets again takes that wire down and gives the coils back.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.rul: A wire is a straight line and needs a clear path. If you later place a block across it, it snaps and drops its coils.
A span can be up to %s blocks long with Coated Wire, less with heavier wire.
One outlet holds up to %s wires.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.cut: Aim a **Wire Cutter** at a span and right click to snip it. Breaking an outlet takes down all its wires. Either way the coils drop.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.tra: A **Transfer Block** is a full block that takes wires on every face. Use them as poles to carry a line a long way, or as junctions to branch it.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_wiring.dis: Right click one with a solid block to disguise it as that block. Sneak and right click it with an empty hand to undo that.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.intr: Every wire has a **limit**, the most power it can carry each tick. Heavier wire carries more, but spans less far.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.char: Bars show how far a span reaches. Bolts show how much power it carries.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.coat: **Coated Wire**: %s SP/t, spans up to %s blocks.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.supe: **Super Heavy Wire**: %s SP/t, up to %s blocks.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.conn: Outlets have limits too. Heavy wire only fits a heavy connector, at both ends.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.outl: **Outlet** and **Transfer Block**: %s SP/t. Coated and Advanced Wire.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.heav: **Heavy Transfer Block**: %s SP/t. Wire up to Super Heavy.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.ulti: **Advanced Outlet** and **Ultimate Transfer Block**: %s SP/t. Wire up to Ultimate.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.teth: **Tether Outlet**: %s SP/t. Every wire, Tether Wire included.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.burn: A wire that carries more than its limit for more than a moment burns away, and its coils are lost. An overloaded outlet burns out too.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.choo: Count the power through each wire, not the whole network. A wire to one furnace only carries that furnace's draw, but the wire next to a big generator or battery bank may carry everything. When power has more than one way to go, it splits between them by how much each wire can carry, so a second wire along another route takes its fair share of the load.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_tiers.tip: Hover a wire or outlet and hold Shift to see its limit. This works here in the guide and in your inventory.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_storage.in: A **Battery** stores spare power and gives it back when your machines want more than your generators make.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_storage.ba: Place battery cells next to each other. Touching cells join into one **bank** of up to %s cells.
Put an outlet on any cell and wire it into your network. The whole bank shares that outlet.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_storage.nu: Each cell holds %s SP and charges at up to %s SP/t. A bank gives back as much as the network needs, all at once.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_storage.or: Whatever is left over charges the batteries.
When the machines want more than the generators make, batteries and generator stores cover the gap.
So batteries fill up in quiet times and help out when everything runs at once. They cannot make power. If they keep running empty, you need more generators.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_storage.st: Most generators also keep a store of their own. It works like a small battery for the network they are on.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_storage.ti: A full bank can push a lot of power down one wire. Make sure the wires next to it can carry that, or put a **Breaker** in the line.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_switches.i: Switch blocks control the power between parts of a network. Put outlets on two or more faces of the switch and wire each one to a different part.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_switches.s: While a switch is **closed**, power flows between its faces. While it is **open**, every face is cut off from the others.
Top: closed, power flows through. Bottom: tripped open, the far side gets nothing.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_switches.b: A **Breaker** stays closed until too much power flows through it. Then it trips open, quickly enough to save the wires.
Right click it to reset it, or to trip it by hand. It gives a redstone signal while it is tripped.
Use an **Auto Reset Upgrade** on it. After an overload it then closes again by itself once the load would be safe.
A breaker trips at the limit of the weakest wire or outlet attached to it.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_switches.c: A **Power Cutoff** opens while it gets a redstone signal. Hook up a lever or any redstone circuit to switch a whole section on and off.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_switches.s: A **Power Sensor** always lets power through. It gives a redstone signal while power flows, and a comparator reads how close the line is to its limit.
An open switch splits a network into separate parts for power. Redstone signals and computer data still cross it, so your controls keep working.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_switches.t: Put a Breaker between a big generator or battery bank and the rest of the base. An overload then trips the breaker instead of burning your wires.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_networks.i: A **network** is everything joined together by wire. Power moves freely inside one network, but never jumps to another one.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_networks.j: Outlets on the same block. Two outlets on one machine, or even on one plain block, are joined. Switches and routers are the exception.
Cells of one battery bank. Outlets on different cells are joined through the bank.
A closed switch joins the outlets on its faces.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_networks.m: Top: two networks. Bottom: one new wire joins them into one.
Link any outlet of one network to any outlet of the other. From then on all their generators and batteries serve all their machines.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_networks.a: No wire between them, or a wire that was cut, snapped or burnt.
An open switch, like a tripped Breaker or a Power Cutoff that gets a signal.
A **Network Router**. Its outlets stay separate networks for power, while data passes between them.
A **Network Hub**. It shares data with far networks, never power.
Unloaded chunks. Power only flows through loaded chunks, so a far section needs a player nearby or a **Chunk Loader**.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_networks.d: Wires also carry data for computers, redstone transmitters and speakers, and data reaches further than power. See **Facility Networks**.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_reading.in: When something seems off, look at what the network is doing. Here is where to find it.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_reading.sc: Most machine screens show a status. **Running** means full power. **Low power** means it gets less than it wants and works slower. **No power** means nothing arrives at all.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_reading.ja: If you play with **Jade**, look at a block to read its power.
**Outlet**: the whole network's supply and demand, its stored power and its number of devices. A red **Low power** line means machines are going short.
**Machine**: its input, what it gets against what it wants.
**Generator**: what it makes, what it sends out and how full its store is.
**Battery**: the size of the bank, its charge, and whether it is charging or discharging.
**Switch**: open, closed or tripped, and its load against its limit.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_reading.sh: Hover any wire, outlet, battery or generator and hold Shift to see its numbers. This also works on the icons in this guide.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_reading.se: Wire a **Power Sensor** into a line. It gives a redstone signal while power flows, and a comparator beside it gets stronger as the line nears its limit.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_reading.ti: Check the outlet closest to a problem first. It shows the whole network that outlet belongs to.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_troublesho: Machine not working? Go through these checks in order.
No power at all
Is there an outlet on the machine itself? An outlet only powers the block it sits on.
Is the wire still there? Wires snap when a block is placed across them and burn when overloaded. Jade shows **Wire: not connected** on a bare outlet.
Does the generator have fuel, sun or steam? Look at it with Jade to see what it makes.
Is a switch open? A tripped Breaker, or a Power Cutoff that gets a signal, cuts the network in two.
Is the whole line loaded? A generator in an unloaded chunk sends nothing.
Low power
Add up what your machines draw and compare it with what your generators make. Jade on any outlet shows both.
Batteries only help until they run empty. If they never get to fill up, build more generators.
Wires keep burning
The wire is too light for the power through it. Use a heavier tier, or add a second wire along another route.
Big generators and full battery banks push far more than Coated Wire can carry. Use heavy wire next to them, or add a Breaker.
A wire will not connect
**Something is in the way**: clear the straight line between the two outlets.
**Too long**: put a Transfer Block in between, or use a lighter wire, which spans further.
**Needs an Advanced Outlet**: heavy wire needs a heavy connector at both ends.
**At most %s wires**: the outlet is full. Add a Transfer Block to branch the line.
A hub shows NO POWER
A Network Hub needs its full %s SP/t every tick. Wire it with Advanced Wire or better, from a generator at its own site.
A hub or router never moves power. If two parts of your base should share power, they need a wire between them.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_power.in: Every wire network carries two things, **power** and **data**. Data is everything else that travels along wires: computer chat, redstone signals, speaker sounds and point banks.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_power.si: Each site runs on its own generator. Hubs carry only data between them.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_power.po: Power only flows along wires inside one network. Nothing else carries it, not a router and not a hub.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_power.da: Across an open switch, so your controls still work while the power is cut.
Through a **Network Router**, between the networks wired to its outlets.
Through a **Network Hub**, to every hub on the same port, at any distance.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_power.de: Redstone Transmitters, Receivers and Port Ranges need some power on their network, but draw none themselves. Computers and hubs draw power like any other machine.
Hover an icon for its name.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_power.ti: Linking two sites with hubs does not let one site's generators run the other site's machines. Build a generator at each site, or run a wire between them.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_energu: A **Block of Energum** is the simplest generator. It needs no fuel, never runs out and gives %s SP/t, forever.
Every block adds %s SP/t, so wire several together for more.
Find **Energum Ore** in ordinary stone underground. It never forms in deepslate. Any stone pickaxe mines it.
Each ore drops a few **Energum Dust**, and Fortune drops more.
Craft nine dust into a **Block of Energum**, place it and put an outlet on it.
One block charges a Block of Redstone into **Charged Redstone** in about %s seconds. That is how every facility gets started.
It is far too weak to run machines at full speed. Use it to build your first **Heat Generator**, then move on.
Keep spare dust. Outlets, batteries, Advanced Wire and many other parts are made with it.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_heat.i: The **Heat Generator** burns furnace fuel for power. It is the first real generator, and building one takes a piece of **Charged Redstone**.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_heat.c: A hopper on top keeps it fed. Power leaves through an outlet.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_heat.s: Place it. It stands two blocks tall, so leave room above.
Fill its three slots with coal, charcoal, wood or any other furnace fuel. A lava bucket lasts longest and comes back empty.
Put an outlet on either half and wire it to your machines.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_heat.o: Each burning slot makes %s SP/t, so all three give %s SP/t. A piece of fuel lasts as long as it would in a furnace.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_heat.s: It keeps up to %s SP in its own store. When that is full the slots stop burning, so no fuel is wasted. When machines want more than it makes, the network draws on the store too.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_heat.a: Hoppers can feed fuel into any side. A hopper underneath pulls out empty buckets but never takes fuel.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_heat.t: One generator runs a couple of small machines. For more power, add generators to the same network or build a steam plant.
A steam plant has three parts. A **Water Boiler** burns fuel to make steam, a **Steam Turbine** turns the steam into power, and a **Cooling Tower** turns used steam back into water.
Boiler, turbine and cooling tower, joined by vents and a water pipe.
Each part is a big machine placed from one item. It builds itself away from you, starting at the block you click, so clear the space first.

Pipe water into the **Water Boiler** and fill its three slots with furnace fuel. It burns fuel %s times faster than a furnace and, once hot, makes %s mB of steam a second. Heating up takes %s seconds.
Run **Vents** from the steam outlet on top of the boiler to the two inlets on top of the **Steam Turbine**. Put an outlet on the turbine's casing and wire it into your network.
Vent the exhaust at the back of the turbine into a **Cooling Tower**, and pipe the water it returns back to the boiler.
Gas and water only move under pressure. Every separate vent line needs a **Vent Pressurizer**, drawing %s SP/t, and every pipe line a **Pipe Pressurizer**, drawing %s SP/t.
A turbine makes up to %s SP/t from %s mB of steam a second and keeps up to %s SP in its store. It only runs at full speed while its inlet is at least half full.
One boiler cannot keep up. It takes %s hot boilers to run one turbine at full speed.
If the turbine's exhaust backs up, it slows down and then stops. A Cooling Tower takes up to %s mB of used steam a second and returns most of it as water. Hot biomes get less back.
Steam is harmless, but any that escapes from an open vent end is lost. Make sure every vent ends at a machine.
**Solar Panels** turn daylight into power with no fuel at all. They need an open view of the sky.
Output peaks at noon and stops at night. The store keeps the network fed after dark.
**Solar Panel**: one block, up to %s SP/t, stores %s SP.
**Solar Array**: a 2x2 frame made from four panels. Up to %s SP/t with a %s SP store, more than four loose panels.
Output follows the sun. It peaks at noon, falls as the sun gets low and stops at night. Rain cuts it, storms cut it more, and shaded parts of an array lose their share.
There is no sun in the Nether or the End, so panels make nothing there.
Put outlets on the terminal plates at the north and south ends. They always face north and south, whichever way you placed the panel.
Pair panels with a **Battery**. Together with the panels' own store, it keeps the lights on through the night.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_oil.in: Crude oil is pumped up from bedrock and refined into fuel for the **Combustion Generator**. Each machine in the chain is a big machine that runs on power.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_oil.ca: Crude oil becomes light and heavy oil, then fuel, then power.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_oil.st: Dig down to bedrock and place an **Oil Extractor** with its wellhead right on it. It pumps %s mB of crude oil a second and draws %s SP/t.
Pipe the crude oil into a **Distillation Tower**. It splits it into Light Oil and Heavy Oil and draws %s SP/t.
A **Chemical Processor** turns Light Oil into Light Fuel and Heavy Oil into Heavy Fuel. It draws %s SP/t.
Pipe the fuel into a **Combustion Generator**. It has its own page next.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_oil.pl: Each machine builds itself away from you, starting at the block you click. Outlets only fit its socket plate. With too little power it just works slower.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_oil.pi: Pipes only move liquid under pressure, so give every pipe line a **Pipe Pressurizer**. An **Oil Refinery** can turn Light Oil into Plastic instead of fuel.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_oil.ti: Crude Oil and Heavy Oil are sticky to wade through, and dumping oil into water pollutes it.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_combus: The **Combustion Generator** burns Light or Heavy Fuel for power. It needs no power itself, but it gives off toxic gas that you must deal with.
The exhaust runs through a pressurized vent into a Gas Dissolver.
Pipe fuel into its left side.
Put an outlet on its socket plate and wire it into your network.
Connect **Vents** to the exhaust on top and put a **Vent Pressurizer** on them. The generator never pushes the gas out by itself.
End the vents at a **Gas Dissolver** topped up with water, or store the gas in a **Gas Tank**.
If the exhaust fills up, the engine stops until the gas is drawn off.
Heavy Fuel makes more power than Light Fuel, but twice as much gas. The generator sends out up to %s SP/t from a store of %s SP and pauses when that is full, so no fuel is wasted.
Gas leaking from an open vent end forms toxic clouds. See **Toxic Waste** in the Safety chapter.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_fusion: The **Fusion Reactor** is the biggest generator. It fuses **Reactive Material** with water and delivers up to %s SP/t.
Power to start it goes in on the left. Power comes out on the right.
Place it from one item. It needs a clear space %s wide, %s deep and %s tall, and builds itself away from you.
Put **Advanced Outlets** on its two side terminals. Seen from the front, the left one takes power in and the right one sends it out.
Wire both with **Ultimate Wire**. The terminals only move as much power as their outlets and wires can carry.
Pipe water into the inlet at the bottom of the back, or pour buckets in. The tank holds %s buckets.
Put **Reactive Material** in its fuel slot. The Irradiation Chamber makes it from Energum Dust.
Press START. The reactor first draws %s SP through the left terminal, at up to %s SP/t. With fuel and at least %s bucket of water it then ignites and runs by itself.
One Reactive Material lasts %s minutes at full output, and it uses %s mB of water every tick. Even with nothing drawing power it slowly burns fuel and water.
If fuel or water runs out it shuts down, and the next start needs the full charge again. Keep a spare in the fuel slot and the tank topped up.
It needs no cooling and makes no waste. Breaking any part takes the whole reactor down, and its water, charge and stored power are lost.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.generator_fissio: The fission reactor is built from towers. It makes no power itself. It boils water into steam for **Steam Turbines**.
Fuel, control rods and coolant side by side. Steam goes to a turbine and toxic gas to a dissolver.
The towers
**Fuel Tower**: one fuel rod per segment. It makes the heat.
**Control Rod Tower**: sets how hard the fuel beside it reacts. Without one, fuel does nothing.
**Coolant Tower**: cools the fuel beside it by boiling water into steam.
**Steam Channel**: makes extra steam from hot fuel without cooling it.
**Booster Tower**: against a rod tower, makes fuel run hotter and burn faster.
**Reactor Controller**: shows the whole reactor and moves every rod.
Building it
Place towers so they touch side by side. Touching towers form one reactor. Stack segments up to %s high. Towers only affect each other on levels that line up.
Right click a Fuel Tower with a **Uranium** or **Thorium Fuel Rod** to load it. At full power a uranium rod lasts %s minutes and a thorium rod %s.
Pipe water into the Coolant Tower and vent its steam from the top to your turbines.
Put a Vent or a **Gas Dissolver** right under the Fuel Tower. Its toxic gas comes out of the bottom.
Right click the Control Rod Tower to pull its rods out a little at a time. Sneak and right click to push them back in.
**Facility notice:** the old Fission Reactor block is decommissioned. It no longer runs and can only be mined to recover what was inside.
A reactor is only as safe as its cooling. Keep an eye on the temperature.
Heat
Rods pulled further out make more heat and more steam. Coolant Towers carry heat away, but only above boiling and only as fast as they can boil water. A Booster makes everything hotter.
From %s °C a tower is **HOT** and burns anyone standing on it. At %s °C it turns **CRITICAL**, scorches everything close by and starts to break down.
A critical tower loses integrity. Cool it below %s °C and it slowly recovers. If integrity runs out the tower explodes, and the blast can heat the towers beside it past their limit.
A tower that explodes with several rods inside spreads clouds of toxic fallout. Keep a gas mask at hand.
Staying in control
A redstone signal on a Control Rod Tower drives its rods fully in for as long as the signal lasts.
The SCRAM button on the Reactor Controller pushes every rod in at once.
A comparator next to the Reactor Controller reads how hot the reactor runs.
Never
Never pull rods out without a Coolant Tower full of water beside the fuel.
Never add Booster Towers without adding cooling to match.
Never block the gas outlet under a Fuel Tower.
Steam that the towers cannot hold vents harmlessly into the air, but the toxic gas does not. Always give it somewhere to go.
Once your first charge is done, pick a generator. Each one has its own page, and the Power chapter explains wiring them up.
Click an icon to open its page.
A **Sterile Swab** works on blocks too. Use it on any surface and read it in the analyzer like any other swab.
A **Disinfecting Wipe** cleans every surface around the block you wipe, and kills anything growing there.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.in: Two machines link your wire network with power from other mods, which is measured in **FE**.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.re: The **Power Receiver** takes FE from other mods and feeds it into your network as SP.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.em: The **Power Emitter** draws SP from your network and gives it out as FE.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.fr: The port on the front is for other mods. Place the bridge against their cable, generator or machine and the port turns to face it. A screwdriver turns it too.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.ba: Put an outlet on any other face and wire it into your network like any other machine.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.ra: %s FE is worth %s SP. Each bridge keeps %s out of every %s that passes through it, so sending power round in a loop always loses some.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.li: A bridge has no small limit of its own. It moves as much as its wires and outlets can carry, up to %s SP/t, and other mods' machines take what they can.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.bu: Each one keeps a small buffer of %s FE so the flow stays smooth.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.power_bridges.ti: Look at a bridge to see how much is flowing. It tells you when nothing is on its front port or when it is not wired to a network.
